name: @argszero/dsh-mcp-tool-filter
description: `dsh-mcp-client` registers every tool a connected MCP server lists, unconditionally, so a server advertising 161 tools puts 161 tools and their full JSON schemas into every request that assembles the tool surface (reported as #9385). `ctx.tools.restrict()` is not the answer: it needs a scoped context, it throws on names that a changed `tools/list` no longer produces, and it only masks a definition that stays registered and introspectable. This plugin shadows `register` on the tools service instance — the one seam that keeps a tool out of the registry entirely — and, for the servers a deployment names, forwards a registration only when the public leaf name is on that server's allowlist. Unlisted servers pass through untouched; an empty allowlist registers nothing from its server; `observe` mode counts what would be kept out without removing anything; the snapshot reports the kept-out names, the configured servers that never matched, and the allowlist entries that never matched anything. Zero runtime dependencies, fail-open, no sandbox changes.
